name: pr-size-labeler
desc: When someone opens a pull request, this bot looks at how much code changed and sticks a size label on it — XS for tiny fixes, XL for monsters. Giant PRs are hard to review, so it gently nudges the author to split them.
notes: Creates the size/* labels automatically
XL threshold is 800+ lines

name: first-touch-welcomer
desc: The first time someone opens an issue or pull request in your project, this bot posts a friendly welcome comment. New contributors feel noticed instead of shouting into the void.
notes: Skips owners, members, and collaborators
First-timer detection via the search API

name: stale-bot
desc: Hunts down issues and pull requests nobody has touched in 30 days, marks them as stale, and closes them a week later if nobody responds. Any comment resets the clock.
notes: Requires REPO=owner/name env var
STALE_DAYS and CLOSE_AFTER_DAYS configurable

name: branch-sweeper
desc: Deletes branches that were merged months ago and are just cluttering up the branch list. It double-checks before deleting anything, and never touches protected branches.
notes: Never touches forks or protected branches (main, develop, release…)

name: conventional-pr-check
desc: Makes sure every pull request title follows the conventional format like 'fix: crash on startup' or 'feat: dark mode'. Keeps your history readable and your changelogs automatic.
notes: Make it a required check in branch protection to block merges

name: reviewer-assigner
desc: Looks at which files a pull request touches and assigns the right reviewers automatically — your own mini-CODEOWNERS, no GitHub Team plan needed.
notes: Configure path prefixes in reviewers.json
Never assigns the PR author

name: duplicate-issue-hunter
desc: When a new issue comes in, this bot searches existing ones and comments if it finds likely duplicates. Saves maintainers from answering the same bug report five times.
notes: Only fires on 2+ keyword overlap — vague issues stay quiet

name: todo-tracker
desc: Watches for new TODO and FIXME comments in the code and opens a tracking issue for each one, so they don't rot in the codebase forgotten. Closes the issue when the TODO is removed.
notes: Dedupes by content hash — no duplicates from merges

name: merge-conflict-detector
desc: Warns you the moment a pull request can no longer merge cleanly because the main branch moved on. Flips the warning to resolved when you fix it.
notes: Retries once after 3s — GitHub computes mergeability async

name: auto-merger
desc: Merges pull requests automatically once they're approved and all checks pass. No more sitting around waiting to click the green button.
events: Pull requests, Check runs, Check suites, Status
notes: Repos without CI count as green
Create the automerge label first

name: repo-digest
desc: Posts a weekly summary issue: what got merged, what opened, what's still waiting. Like a newspaper for your repository.
notes: Requires REPO=owner/name env var

name: pr-template-checker
desc: Checks that pull request authors actually filled in the template instead of leaving the placeholder text. Reminds them politely if they didn't.
notes: REQUIRED_SECTIONS env var, e.g. 'summary,test plan'

name: release-drafter
desc: Keeps a draft release up to date as pull requests merge, grouped by change type. When it's time to ship, your release notes are already written.
notes: Groups entries by conventional-commit prefix
Publish the draft whenever you cut a release

name: keyword-issue-labeler
desc: Reads new issues and labels them based on what they mention — 'crash' gets the bug label, 'feature request' gets enhancement. Instant triage with zero effort.
notes: Configurable keyword → label map in labels.json
Ships with sensible defaults

name: ci-failure-commenter
desc: When CI fails on a pull request, this bot posts a compact comment explaining what broke, with links to the logs. Updates the same comment when it goes green again.
notes: Collapses repeat failures into one updated comment

name: pr-aging-bot
desc: Flags pull requests that have been sitting open too long without review. Old PRs die in silence; this makes them visible.
notes: Skips drafts by default (SKIP_DRAFTS=false to include)
Only writes when a PR crosses a tier boundary
Run nightly as a GitHub Action or crontab

name: review-reminder
desc: Nudges reviewers who were asked to review but haven't responded. Escalates politely as days pass.
notes: REMIND_AFTER_HOURS configures the wait (default 24)
Tracks reminders via managed comment markers

name: issue-triage-reminder
desc: Reminds maintainers about new issues that nobody has labeled or answered. Nothing slips through the cracks.
notes: GRACE_HOURS configures the grace period (default 24)
Self-cleaning: label removed when a human triages

name: changelog-checker
desc: Reminds authors to update the changelog when their pull request changes user-facing behavior. No more forgotten entries at release time.
notes: CHANGELOG_FILE and SKIP_LABEL are configurable
Re-evaluates when labels change

name: license-header-checker
desc: Checks that new source files carry the project's license header. Keeps you compliant without manual review.
perms: statuses: write, pulls: read, issues: write
notes: HEADER_TEXT and SOURCE_EXTENSIONS configurable
Only checks newly added files, not existing ones

name: pr-path-labeler
desc: Labels pull requests by which part of the codebase they touch — frontend, backend, docs — so you can filter work by area.
notes: Optional path-labels.json for explicit prefix→label mapping
Never invents labels — only applies ones that already exist

name: contributor-milestones
desc: Celebrates contributors when they hit milestones — first PR merged, tenth, fiftieth. Small celebrations keep people coming back.
notes: Recognition drives repeat contribution
Bot accounts are ignored

name: breaking-change-guard
desc: Flags pull requests that look like they break existing behavior, so they get extra scrutiny before merging.
perms: statuses: write, pulls: read, issues: write
notes: Detects feat!: titles and BREAKING CHANGE footers
Re-checks on label changes so acknowledgment flips it green

name: release-reminder
desc: Nags you when lots of unreleased work has piled up on the main branch. A gentle push to actually ship.
notes: THRESHOLD_COMMITS sets the trigger (default 20)
Updates one managed issue instead of spamming

name: docs-link-checker
desc: Checks links in your documentation and README, and reports the dead ones. Nothing embarrasses like a 404 in the getting-started guide.
notes: Concurrent link checking with per-URL caching
HEAD-then-GET fallback for picky servers

name: issue-link-checker
desc: Verifies links people paste into issues actually work. Dead reproduction links get flagged automatically.
notes: Skips github.com links to save rate quota
Edits re-check, comment updates in place

name: issue-form-validator
desc: Makes sure new issues follow your template — a bug report without steps to reproduce gets a friendly request to fill it in properly.
notes: REQUIRED_SECTIONS configures which headings must be filled
Rejects placeholder content, not just empty sections

name: dependency-update-grouper
desc: Groups the flood of dependabot pull requests into batches so you review them once a week instead of every single day.
notes: Exactly one deps/* label per PR
Pairs well with auto-merger: auto-merge deps/patch only

name: flaky-test-tracker
desc: Notices when the same test fails intermittently across runs and files a tracking issue. Flaky tests stop being invisible.
notes: FLAKE_THRESHOLD controls sensitivity (default 3)
State persisted in flaky-state.json

name: merge-queue-assistant
desc: Shows which pull request is next in line to merge, labeling the queue so everyone knows the order.
notes: Oldest queued PR is always the head
Head merging or closing promotes the next in line automatically

name: discussion-triage-bot
desc: Flags discussions that have been sitting unanswered. Questions from your community deserve replies.
notes: Uses the GraphQL API — discussions aren't in REST
Verified live against github-bot-store itself

name: project-board-sync
desc: Keeps your GitHub project board in sync automatically — new issues and PRs land on the board, status follows the work.
perms: issues: read, pulls: read, projects: write
notes: Assigned work moves to In Progress, closed/merged to Done
GraphQL-powered; degrades gracefully if the board has no Status field
